# omadafusion_static_route (Resource)

A gateway static route (Network Config > Routing > Static Route), next-hop type. Names must be unique. The controller does not report `interface_id` back, so changes to it made outside Terraform are not detected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "omadafusion_lan_network" "management" { name = "Management" }

# Reach a lab network behind a router on the management LAN.
resource "omadafusion_static_route" "lab" {
  name         = "Lab"
  destinations = ["10.99.0.0/16"]
  next_hop     = "192.168.10.254"
  interface_id = data.omadafusion_lan_network.management.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destinations` (List of String) Destination networks in CIDR form.
- `interface_id` (String) Outgoing interface: a WAN port UUID or LAN network ID.
- `name` (String) Route name. Must be unique.
- `next_hop` (String) Next-hop IPv4 address.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the route is active.
- `metric` (Number) Metric, 0-15.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Route ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id> or <site>/<id>. interface_id is not returned by the controller; set it in config after import.
terraform import omadafusion_static_route.lab Default/64f0c0ffee00000000000001
```
